items.claim: pathDistanceToPoint measures a negative-size RectPath as if the point were outside it
mergeRegion with `tolerance: 0` drops every piece and returns an empty path
mergeRegion leaves a gap mid-contour where two or more consecutive sub-`snap` straight edges are dropped, and the merged output gains chords across the shape
snipPathAt removes two pieces when the probe's nearest point is exactly a crossing, and a closed subpath crossed once comes back in `removed` drawn twice
roughenPath's seed is truncated to an int32, so fractional seeds all roughen the same way
joinPaths takes its origin from the first part only, so a far part loses float32 precision

items.note: Question: no one has ruled on what happens when the open parts disagree on `openFill`. I made the strict call: the first open part's rule wins and it warns. It is recorded in `docs/unruled.md` (4217d260dd).

items.claim: translatePath leaves an origin-free polygon moved far from 0 in raw float32, where transformPath gives it an origin
reachToMeet in `'curvature'` mode on a straight end grows an infinite line and finds nothing
splitByClosure puts corner specs one anchor off after a subpath that starts without an `M`
simplifyAnchorsAt rotates a closed subpath so it starts on a different anchor
mergeRegion reads its winding from an area that depends on `openFill`, though it treats every subpath as closed
solveSpiro forces the tangent at a point next to a coincident neighbor to +X
schneiderFit breaks the tangent at every split, and a repeated sample pins a handle onto its anchor
roundRectPath with 0 corner samples and circlePath with 0 segments build NaN or empty geometry
items.note: Question: this needed a behavior call. I made the strict one: both throw `RangeError` instead of clamping. It is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: mergeRegion leaves a ring open where three edges cross at one point, then closes it with a chord
items.note: The test reproduced the failure before the fix: edges were left inside the fill.

items.claim: growRegion has the same winding mistake as mergeRegion, taking its offset side from the `openFill`-dependent area
items.note: in the same commit as mergeRegion's.
